major_concerns: Intent set may be synthetic / insufficiently representative of enterprise heterogeneity (external validity).
Validator/emulator fidelity mismatch with real devices can bias safety estimates.
Potential model/API outages or rate limits could force post‑hoc deviations.
Risk of overclaiming cross‑vendor generality from a limited emulator/validator setup.
required_design_repairs: Broaden intent corpus to include vendor‑diverse, real‑world ticket templates or clearly justify synthetic sampling; stratify results by vendor/topology.
Explicitly quantify validator coverage (which properties checked) and add tests to estimate validator false‑negative rate (validator misses).
Define contingency plan and logging for API outages and enforce preregistered call budget; record any deviations.
Add explicit emulator→realism discussion and, where possible, include cross‑validator consistency checks (e.g., Batfish + NetKAT comparisons).

major_concerns: Adversarial corpus construction risks producing harmful payloads—safety and legal concerns.
Attack models may not map to realistic attacker capabilities (external validity).
Reproducibility is sensitive to exact poisoning heuristics and retrieval implementation details.
Defenses tuned to one LLM may not generalize; single‑model reliance weakens claims.
required_design_repairs: Mandate sanitization and non‑execution of any generated commands; include strict text filters and human‑review blocks for potentially harmful content.
Define and justify attacker capabilities and budgets; include at least two distinct poisoning strategies to increase coverage.
Publish exact poisoning scripts, retrieval index snapshots, and seed values to enable replication; provide checksums.
Evaluate defenses across at least two LLM variants or simulate transferability to show generality; report model‑dependence.

major_concerns: Construct validity: simulated reviewer (LLM proxy) may not reflect real human operator detection patterns.
Calibration corpus and procedure are underspecified and may bias reviewer behavior.
Risk of overgeneralizing from simulated to human oversight effectiveness.
required_design_repairs: Substantially strengthen reviewer calibration: document corpora, metrics, and calibration experiments; include sensitivity analyses across reviewer model families and temps.
Avoid claims about real human operators; limit conclusions to simulated‑reviewer proxies and explicitly state construct limitations.
If possible within constraints, include a small human spot‑check (public volunteer or expert) or cite external human‑review studies to triangulate simulated reviewer behavior.
Report reviewer decision latency model and justify time‑budget simulation parameters with operational citations.

major_concerns: Schema/template design may unfairly advantage constrained approach or fail to cover vendor syntax nuances.
Automated intent‑fulfillment oracle may misclassify novel but correct free‑form solutions (construct validity).
Parser/regeneration loops may inflate token usage and affect feasibility within budget.
required_design_repairs: Define and publish vendor‑specific schema/templates (or use multiple vendors) and report per‑vendor outcomes.
Validate the automated oracle with human spot checks on a stratified sample to verify scoring rubric.
Measure and report token/time costs for parser/regeneration loops and include these in feasibility analysis; predefine maximum re‑generation attempts.
Include analyses of cases where schema prevents valid solutions and report techniques to relax schemas while preserving validator pass rates.
